previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and homelessness was admitted for right flank pain. She expressed regret for leaving a prior admission early and wished to stay for full evaluation. Workup showed no evidence of nephrolithiasis or pyelonephritis on renal ultrasound, and labs did not support active infection despite a positive urine culture likely reflecting colonization. Blood cultures did not show recurrent Corynebacterium bacteremia. Flank pain improved with NSAIDs and acetaminophen with codeine. She was treated with a single dose of fluconazole for vaginal candidiasis and continued home medications for frostbite. Social work secured shelter placement. She was discharged home with naproxen for pain and instructions to return if symptoms worsened.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o F with PMHx of neurogenic bladder w/ chronic indwelling 
foley, h.o. UTI/Pyelonephritis p/w acute history of fevers, Left 
CV tenderness diagnosed with Multidrug resistant E. Coli 
Cystitis. 

##. Bacterial Cystitis: Pt was admitted from the ED for 
suspected pyelonephritis given her history of fevers, left CV 
tenderness and U/A suspicious for infection. Pt was started on 
IV Ceftriaxone initially and then transitioned to Cefpodoxime. 
On ___ day of admission pt was noted to have a urine positive 
for E. Coli that was multidrug resistance, sensitive only to 
Nitrofurantoin, Tobramycin and Meropenem. Given lack of fevers, 
CV tenderness and quick resolution of leukocytosis on a regimen 
that infection was resistant to presentation more likely to be 
bacterial cystitis as opposed to Pyelonephritis. After 
discussion with ID pt was discharged with a regimen of 
Nitrofurantoin and set up for a new PCP ___. Pt was set 
up for a repeat culture as an outpatient prior to her new PCP 
appointment to ensure clearance of E. Coli on Nitrofurantoin.

## Neurogenic bladder:  Ms. ___ has a neurogenic bladder 
following a gun shot wound to the spine at the age of ___, she 
has had a chronic indwelling catheter since that time. During 
hospitaliztion discussion was initiated regarding the 
possibility of a suprapubic catheter given it's lower risk of 
infection when compared to an indwelling catheter. According to 
the pt the possibility of a suprapubic catheter was discussed 
several years ago, unfortunately as she has not been able to see 
a physician no further work has been done. I discussed with the 
pt in depth the importance of inquiring about a suprapubic 
catheter with her new PCP; particularly given the increased 
pattern of resistance of her E. Coli organism.

years, she was originally seen at ___. A new

___.
